paragraphs.text: GitMate — a smart Git panel for DeepSeek Harness: diffs, generated commit messages, a commit graph w
ith rewind, and .gitignore generation, plus ten agent tools.
# GitMate
**A Git panel in the DeepSeek Harness sidebar — plus the same operations as fifteen agent tools.**
Runs anywhere the Harness does: macOS, Linux, and Windows (PowerShell).
Only two things genuinely differ across platforms, and both live on the Host side: **how arguments a
re quoted** (PowerShell doubles a single quote, a POSIX shell closes-escapes-reopens; chosen by `pro
cess.platform`) and **how the environment is passed** (through the shell request's `env` field rathe
r than a POSIX `VAR=value` prefix, which is not a command on Windows). Nothing else is platform-awar
e: paths go through `node:path`, nothing outside `lib/` is written, and no file needing an executabl
e bit is created. When the sandbox will not start, the advice **names the cause for the platform you
are on** (bubblewrap/Landlock on Linux, `sandbox-exec` on macOS, `%TEMP%` on Windows).
English | 中文
Review changes, read diffs, stage, commit with a generated message, merge, stash, sync, and rewind h
istory without leaving the panel. Every operation is also a tool the agent can call, so asking in ch
t leaving the panel. Every operation is also a tool the agent can call, so asking in chat works too.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH once, refresh the page, then open **GitMate** from the sidebar's **+** menu.
> The internal ids (Loader row `dsh-git`, tab key) differ from the package name on purpose: the row
id is the key of a config row you may already have, and renaming it would orphan your saved settings
d is the key of a config row you may already have, and renaming it would orphan your saved settings.
## Reviewing and committing
- **Four groups** — conflicts, staged, changes, untracked. Each row shows the kind in words, the pat
h, and that file's `+N −M`. Row actions stage, unstage, and discard, with a second click for anythin

g destructive.
- **Diffs like an editor** — two line-number gutters, `+`/`−` markers, tinted rows, a
nd only the changed span of a replaced line marked. Click a file to expand it in place; click again

to collapse. Widen the context from 3 lines to 24 when a hunk needs more of the file.
- **One row of

list actions**, shown only when they would do something, with the counts in the labels.
- **Amend**
— fold the staged changes into the previous commit; leaving the message box empty keeps the existin

g message.
- **A draggable splitter** between the list and the commit card resizes the message box.
- **A panel that is working says so** — every operation shows a turning indicator and names itself (
"Committing…", "Reviewing the staged changes…") instead of only greying its buttons out. It sits wit
h the messages at the foot of the list, above the splitter, so it never covers the commit box.
## AI features
| Feature | What it does |
| **Commit message** | Generated from the staged diff. If you have already typed something, the butt
on becomes *Refine draft*: the model keeps your intent and fills in the rest instead of replacing it

. |
| **Review before commit** | Reads the staged changes and reports only what would bite — a wrong
result, a missed edge case, an unhandled error, a committed secret, debug output left in, a behavio

ur change with no test. Click a finding to open that file's diff. |
| **Split this commit** | Divide
s the staged changes into commits that each stand on their own, with a message for each. The plan is
a draft you can edit: rewrite any message, merge a group into the one above, remove one, ask for a
new plan, commit one group at a time, or commit them all in order. Each commit leaves the other file

s staged. |
| **Explain a change** | Two to five bullets on what a file's change does, so you can re

view without reading every line. |
| **Image and PDF preview** | Images and PDFs have no patch to re
ad — git reports them as binary — so opening one reads the **current working-tree file** and shows i
t: `png`/`jpg`/`jpeg`/`gif`/`webp`/`avif`/`bmp`/`ico`/`svg`/`pdf`. 6 MB per file, over which the pan
el says the size instead of forcing it through. Working tree only: the committed copy would have to
come back through a shell as text and would be mangled, so a file that is only staged, or deleted, s

ays plainly that there is nothing to preview. |
| **`.gitignore`** | Infers the rules from the proje
ct's manifests and layout. One button creates it; one adds what is missing **and tidies the whole fi
le** — exact duplicates, rules an earlier broader rule already covers (`node_modules/.cache/` after
`node_modules/`), and runs of blank lines. It groups entries under headings only when that cannot ch
ange the meaning: with a `!` rule (git decides by the last match, so order is semantic) or with your
own comments, the order is kept and the panel says so. |
Buttons that call a model are marked **AI**. Every generation uses the session's default model — the
re is no second model to configure.
## Branches, history, remotes
- **Branch selector** — switch, create, delete, and merge any branch into the checked-out one. A con

flicted merge is reported with the files that need a decision, and can be aborted.
- **Commit graph*
* — every branch and remote-tracking branch, not just this one. Strokes are computed on the Host and
shipped with the data, so "the rows join up" is an assertion rather than something to eyeball. Two
things make it hold:
- **The straight runs are elements pinned to the row's bottom**, not coordinates inside a fixed-heig
ht box. A row's height is not fixed — expanding a commit makes it much taller — and a fixed box left

a gap between every pair of rows, which is what made the tree look like it was floating.
- **When s
everal lanes wait for the same commit, all but the claimed one are released.** Otherwise they keep w
aiting for a commit already emitted and drag a line to the bottom with no commit on it — the other h
alf of the floating look.
A branch opening here starts **below** the node and one converging here arrives **above** it, each j
oined to the node by a curve; one hue carries three weights — the commit's own line, the branch curv
es, and the lanes merely passing through. Expand a commit for its full message, the files it touched
, and what you can do to it: rewind, revert, cherry-pick, rebase, or tag. Click a changed file to se

e its diff inside that commit.
